raw_responses.Bulgarian: The figure presents a bar chart comparing two data series, "Per-Output" and "Per-Layer," across varying sparsity rates. The horizontal axis represents the sparsity rate, labeled as "Sparsity Rate," and displays values ranging from 10% to 80% in increments of 10%. The vertical axis, labeled "Perplexity," uses a logarithmic scale with a base of 10, indicated by the tick marks and corresponding power-of-ten labels (10⁰, 10¹, 10², etc.). The data series "Per-Output" is represented by blue bars, while "Per-Layer" is represented by orange bars. The bars are arranged in ascending order of sparsity rate. The lowest "Per-Output" bar at 10% sparsity has a value approximately around 1, while the highest "Per-Output" bar at 80% sparsity has a value around 20. The lowest "Per-Layer" bar at 10% sparsity has a value approximately around 1, while the highest "Per-Layer" bar at 80% sparsity has a value around 50. Both data series show an increasing trend as the sparsity rate increases.
raw_responses.Chinese: The figure presents a comparison of two data series, "Per-Output" and "Per-Layer," across varying sparsity rates. The chart type is a grouped bar graph. The horizontal axis, labeled "Sparsity Rate," displays categories ranging from 10% to 80%, incrementing by 10% intervals. The vertical axis, labeled "Perplexity," is a logarithmic scale with a base of 10, ranging from 10^0 to 10^3. The vertical axis is marked with tick marks at 1, 10, 100, and 1000. The "Per-Output" data series is represented by blue bars, while the "Per-Layer" data series is represented by orange bars. The bars are grouped side-by-side for each sparsity rate. The blue bars have approximate heights of 1.2, 1.5, 2.1, 2.5, 2.8, 3.3, and 4.2, respectively, corresponding to the sparsity rates of 10%, 20%, 30%, 40%, 50%, 60%, and 80%. The orange bars have approximate heights of 1.5, 2.2, 3.1, 4.1, 5.3, 6.8, and 8.8, respectively, corresponding to the same sparsity rates. The bars are arranged in ascending order of sparsity rate, and no bars are visually emphasized.
raw_responses.English: The chart illustrates the perplexity values for two different approaches, "Per-Output" and "Per-Layer," across varying sparsity rates. The horizontal axis represents the sparsity rate, labeled as "Sparsity Rate," and is divided into categories ranging from 10% to 80%, incrementing by 10%. The vertical axis is labeled "Perplexity" and uses a logarithmic scale with a base of 10, ranging from 10^0 to 10^3. Two data series are presented as bars: "Per-Output" is represented by blue bars, and "Per-Layer" is represented by orange bars. The bars are grouped side-by-side for each sparsity rate, allowing for a visual comparison between the two approaches at each level. The shortest blue bar, corresponding to a sparsity rate of 10%, has an approximate value of 1, while the tallest blue bar, at 80% sparsity, has an approximate value of 100. Similarly, the shortest orange bar at 10% sparsity has an approximate value of 1, and the tallest orange bar at 80% sparsity has an approximate value of 100. The bars are sorted in ascending order based on the sparsity rate. No bars are visually emphasized with shading, bolding, outlining, or annotations.
raw_responses.German: The figure presents a bar chart comparing "Per-Output" and "Per-Layer" perplexity values across varying sparsity rates. The vertical axis, labeled "Perplexity," uses a logarithmic scale with a base of 10, ranging from 10^0 to 10^3. Two data series are represented by bars: "Per-Output" is depicted in blue, and "Per-Layer" is shown in orange. The "Per-Output" series exhibits bars with values approximately ranging from 1.2 to 120, while the "Per-Layer" series shows values approximately ranging from 1.5 to 150. The bars for both series increase in length as the sparsity rate increases, with the 80% sparsity rate showing the highest values for both series. The bars are not sorted in any particular order beyond the order of the sparsity rates on the x-axis. No specific bars are visually highlighted.
